title: 2008 Oklahoma Offense: 716 Points and Five Straight 60-Point Games
question: Which Oklahoma team scored the most points in a college football season?
answer: The 2008 Sooners scored 716 points, then the NCAA Division I single-season record, and became the first team since Tulsa in 1919 to score 60 or more points in five straight games.
summary: Oklahoma's 2008 offense scored 716 points and hit 60 in five straight games, led by Heisman winner Sam Bradford. Here's the record-setting run, game by game.
body: Oklahoma has had plenty of great offenses, but nothing in college football at the time matched the 2008 Sooners. Led by sophomore quarterback Sam Bradford, Bob Stoops' team finished the season with 716 points, the most ever by a Division I team up to that point.

The late-season stretch is what people remember. Oklahoma beat Nebraska 62-28, Texas A&M 66-28, Texas Tech 65-21 and Oklahoma State 61-41. Then came the Big 12 Championship Game against Missouri at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City on Dec. 6, 2008, and the Sooners won 62-21. According to STATS LLC, no team had scored at least 60 points in five straight games since Tulsa in 1919.

That night in Kansas City, Bradford threw for 384 yards and two touchdowns and set Big 12 title game records for passing yards and completions. Running back Chris Brown ran for more than 100 yards and three scores. The win gave Oklahoma its third straight conference championship and pushed the Sooners past Hawaii's 2006 NCAA record of 656 points.

Bradford won the Heisman Trophy, the fifth Sooner to do so, after leading the nation with 50 touchdown passes and a 180.8 passer rating. The season ended with a 24-14 loss to Florida in the BCS title game, and Oklahoma finished 12-2. Florida State eventually broke the 716-point record in 2013, but the 2008 Sooners still own a special place in the program's record book.
